next_question: Should the Physics lane proceed with URL-only PMI on the validated hash-SPA testbeds (vanillajs/react/vue/angular/svelte at NL scale, 64–70 raw per variant for 50 NL), or first survey production SPAs with history-based routing for joint (low-leakage, varying-title) sites that could enable title-aware PMI?
why_next: This experiment closes the SPA infrastructure question: hash-SPAs have 21–28% leakage (far below the 40% threshold), making URL-level NL collection feasible at 64–70 raw transitions per 50 NL. The SPA pivot from the parent handoff is justified. However, title-aware PMI is falsified on TodoMVC (0/5 variants have ≥2 titles, replicating EXP-PHYSICS-34266105229 degeneracy). Two paths remain: (1) test URL-only PMI at NL scale on the validated hash-SPA testbeds to directly probe C-WEB-DYNAMICS predictive dynamical structure, or (2) survey production SPAs for title variation before committing to a PMI approach. The highest-information next step depends on whether title-varying SPAs exist — if they do, title-aware PMI may add information beyond URL-only; if not, URL-only PMI at NL scale is the only viable path. Either way, the dominant synthetic-to-real gap is now addressable: the infrastructure barrier (insufficient NL transitions) is removed.

established: Hash-SPA TodoMVC variants exhibit valid-only leakage 0.213–0.285 (5/5 <40%) on the frozen 24-action Playwright protocol; all-raw leakage 0.25 identical across 4/5 variants (vue 0.213 valid-only due to higher error exclusion). Achievable NL at 500 raw: 357–394 (50 NL needs 64–70 raw). (result.json metrics, audit.json recomputed_metrics)

Per-type stratification is perfectly separated on every SPA: link_click leakage 1.00 (170/170 valid), button_click/form_submit/js_navigate leakage 0.00 (548/548 valid). Leakage is entirely action-mix dependent; the 21–28% headline rate reflects the frozen protocol's 27% link share, not a site constant. (result.json metrics, audit.json V1)

Fragment-stripping normalization (strip fragment, trailing slash, percent-encoding) makes link_click leakage tautological on hash-SPAs: all filter links (#/active, #/completed) normalize to the same base path as url_after. (audit.json V3, analyze_spa_survey.py:normalize_url)

Document.title is constant on all 5 TodoMVC variants across all 840 SPA transitions (unique_titles=1, entropy 0.0 bits). Title-aware PMI is NOT viable on TodoMVC. Pipeline validated by 5 distinct Wikipedia titles (entropy 2.32 bits) on the same code path. (result.json metrics, audit.json V2)

Wikipedia (server-rendered MPA control): valid-only leakage 1.00 (100/100 link clicks), 5 distinct titles, 5 distinct normalized URLs. Confirms measurement pipeline correctly identifies high leakage on known MPAs. (result.json controls.NULL_CTRL_WIKIPEDIA)
Zero Playwright EPIPE crashes across 40 sessions (7 per SPA × 5 + 5 wiki) using per-session browser lifecycle mitigation. (result.json observations, provenance.json)
rejected: Title-aware PMI on TodoMVC hash-SPAs: ALL variants have constant document.title (0/5 ≥2 titles, entropy 0.0 bits on 840 transitions). Replicates EXP-PHYSICS-34266105229 degeneracy. Falsified, not merely untested. (result.json metrics, audit.json V2)
TodoMVC as title-varying testbed for C-WEB-DYNAMICS: unique_titles=1 on all variants; URL+title isomorphic to URL-only. (audit.json claim_ceiling)
The preregistered hypothesis that hash-SPA variants would have ≥2 unique document.title values (prereg section 12, expected outcomes): 0/5 variants satisfy this. (spec.json falsifier clause 2)
unknown: Whether production SPAs with history-based (non-hash) routing exhibit URL-level leakage <40% enabling ≥50 NL transitions — only hash routing tested.
Whether any production SPA exists with joint (low leakage <40%, ≥2 unique titles varying independently of URL path) — TodoMVC title-variance untested on production.
Whether URL-only PMI at NL scale on hash-SPAs detects predictive dynamical structure beyond memory (the core C-WEB-DYNAMICS claim) — infrastructure now ready but not yet tested.
Whether per-URL title variance (titles varying independently of path, not just globally diverse titles across sessions) exists on any real SPA.
Whether the PMI pipeline can detect predictive structure on genuinely stochastic production SPA transitions (all prior PMI tests are synthetic or locally-hosted).
do_not_assume: Do NOT assume hash-SPA leakage 0.21–0.28 generalizes to history-routed production SPAs — only hash routing with fragment-stripping normalization tested; history-routed SPAs may have different leakage profiles.
Do NOT assume title constancy is universal across all SPAs — only TodoMVC tested; production SPAs with dynamic page titles may exist.
Do NOT assume URL-level PMI is production-ready — validated only on TodoMVC hash-SPAs with Playwright headless Chrome collection; real-browser auth/session/drift untested.
Do NOT assume the headline leakage rate 0.21–0.28 is an intrinsic site property — it reflects the frozen 27% link-click protocol mix; changing action mix changes headline rate.

Do NOT assume C-WEB-DYNAMICS is tested by this experiment — it concerns predictive dynamical structure beyond memory; this experiment characterizes infrastructure viability (leakage), not the core claim.
Do NOT assume normalized URL entropy 0.0 bits means no state information — it reflects fragment-stripping normalization, not genuine URL constancy (raw URLs have fragments #/active, #/completed).
Do NOT assume title-aware PMI is impossible on all SPAs — only falsified on TodoMVC; production SPAs with dynamic titles remain untested.

recommended_action: Two-materially-orthogonal paths: (A) Test URL-only PMI at NL scale on the 5 validated hash-SPA testbeds (64–70 raw per variant for 50 NL transitions) to directly probe C-WEB-DYNAMICS predictive dynamical structure beyond memory on production-like SPA transitions. This is the highest-information next step because the infrastructure barrier is removed and it addresses the dominant synthetic-to-real gap. (B) Before PMI design, survey 3–5 production SPAs with history-based routing (React Router, Vue Router, Angular Router SPAs) for joint (leakage <40%, ≥2 unique titles varying independently of URL path) — if such sites exist, title-aware PMI may add information beyond URL-only; if not, commit to URL-only PMI path. Path A is lower-risk and higher-velocity; Path B is higher-upside if title-varying SPAs exist but carries survey cost and uncertain discovery.
